core.title: Bind every guarded alt/opt branch fragment to acceptances, and back
core.given: An artifact of the plan-artifact kind named by roles.plan_artifact.kinds contains guarded branch fragments (alt/opt) or flow-branch acceptances (changed or not)
core.when: The planner authors or edits the artifact, or the plan reaches the confirm phase
core.then: Bind both ways: every guarded alt/opt branch fragment references at least one acceptance, and every flow-branch acceptance references back the guard/fragment it covers.
prefer: Give fragments and guards stable ids, and list the acceptance references on each fragment
On each flow-branch acceptance, cite the guard or fragment id it covers
avoid: Guarded alt/opt branch fragments with no acceptance
Flow-branch acceptances bound to no guard or fragment
One-way binding: references on fragments without back-references, or the reverse
Binding a fragment to an unrelated or placeholder acceptance just to pass the check
core.why: Bidirectional binding keeps branches traceable. Each guarded fragment points to its acceptances, and each branch acceptance points to the fragment it covers.
evidence: Every guarded alt/opt branch fragment has at least one acceptance reference that resolves to an existing acceptance
Every flow-branch acceptance has a guard/fragment back-reference that resolves to an existing guard or fragment
verification: Coverage-style validation, run at the confirm phase and confirm-blocking: the check covers every artifact of the designated plan-artifact kind, including unchanged ones
Severity 4; disposition: strict — a missing binding in either direction is a violation; the rule declares no exceptions
One bidirectional binding check, not two: a finding reports the artifact, the fragment, the guard, the acceptance reference, and which side of the binding is missing

A binding counts only if its reference resolves — the fragment's acceptance reference to an existing acceptance, the flow-branch acceptance's back-reference to an existing guard or fragment; the rule imposes no locality restriction on where the target lives

The automated check verifies existence and resolution of references; it does not verify that a referenced acceptance genuinely covers the fragment, so binding to an unrelated or placeholder acceptance is an authoring anti-pattern the check cannot fully detect
Change and term signals are discovery aids only and never a required gate: the gate is the confirm-phase check, which applies changed or not

values: the plan-artifact kind named by roles.plan_artifact.kinds
an artifact of the designated kind contains a guarded alt/opt branch fragment or a flow-branch acceptance
guarded alt/opt branch fragment added or edited

fires: At confirm, an artifact of the designated plan-artifact kind contains guarded alt/opt branch fragments or flow-branch acceptances, including ones not changed in this plan
The planner adds a guarded alt or opt branch fragment to the artifact and must list its acceptance(s)
The planner writes a flow-branch acceptance and must reference back the guard/fragment it covers
An edit removes a guarded fragment's only bound acceptance
doesNotFire: Artifacts of the designated kind with no guarded alt/opt branch fragments and no flow-branch acceptances (linear flow only)
Acceptances for the main linear flow that are not flow-branch acceptances
Artifacts that are not of the designated plan-artifact kind

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact kind whose guarded alt/opt branch fragments and flow-branch acceptances must be bidirectionally bound; the core's given, activation facts, fires and doesNotFire refer to it as 'the designated plan-artifact kind'

neutralityNotes: The convention is about plan-artifact content, not code structure, so almost everything is already stack-neutral; the only concrete datum the core needs is the plan-artifact kind name ('interlocking'), supplied by roles.plan_artifact.kinds (no proposed key needed). Kept Bun-only: the validator id (evidence[0]), validation family/template/variant ids (verifier_detail[0]), failure-evidence field names (verifier_detail[4]) and the term id (verifier_detail[5]). 'alt/opt fragment', 'guard', 'flow branch', 'acceptance' and the confirm phase are treated as neutral plan-artifact schema and workflow vocabulary, since the vocabulary's urn/roles groups already treat ATDD plan concepts as profile data only where they name the stack's artifact kinds. Per-rule severity, strict disposition and confirm-blocking enforcement live in core.verification per the notProfileKeys rule. The Bun notes' crucial scoping (check covers unchanged artifacts too; change/term signals never gate; references must resolve; no locality restriction) are all preserved in core.verification so the instantiated core is neither weaker nor stronger.
